2 Peter 1.summary: Simon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ, writes to them that have obtained like precious faith, with grace and peace multiplied through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord (2 Peter 1:1–2). His divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, and exceeding great and precious promises, that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust (2 Peter 1:3–4). Giving all diligence, they are to add to their faith virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, and charity, for if these things be in them and abound, they make them neither barren nor unfruitful, but he that lacketh these things is blind (2 Peter 1:5–9). They are to give diligence to make their calling and election sure, for so an entrance shall be ministered unto them abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ (2 Peter 1:10–11). Peter will not be negligent to put them in remembrance, knowing that shortly he must put off his tabernacle, even as the Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed him, and will endeavour that they may have these things in remembrance after his decease (2 Peter 1:12–15). The apostles have not followed cunningly devised fables, but were eyewitnesses of his majesty, when he received from God the Father honour and glory, and a voice came from the excellent glory, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased, which they heard in the holy mount (2 Peter 1:16–18). They have a more sure word of prophecy, whereunto they do well to take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, for no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation, but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost (2 Peter 1:19–21).
2 Peter 1.whereWeAre: 2 Peter follows 1 Peter. Simon Peter, knowing his tabernacle will soon be put off, tells believers to add virtue, knowledge, and charity to their faith, reminds them that the apostles were eyewitnesses of Christ's majesty, and points them to the sure word of prophecy (1:1-21). Chapter 2 warns of false teachers.

keyFigures.name: Them that have obtained like precious faith

keyFigures.name: Jesus Christ
keyFigures.role: Our Lord and Saviour, with the power and coming of whom they were made acquainted, and who shewed Peter his death was near (1:1,14,16).

keyFigures.name: God the Father
keyFigures.role: Gave Christ honour and glory, and a voice from the excellent glory said This is my beloved Son (1:17-18).

keyFigures.name: The apostles
keyFigures.role: Eyewitnesses of his majesty who heard the voice in the holy mount (1:16-18).

keyFigures.name: Holy men of God

keyThemes.explanation: His divine power hath given us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, and exceeding great and precious promises, that we might be partakers of the divine nature (1:3-4).
They are to add to faith virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, and charity, that they be neither barren nor unfruitful (1:5-9).

keyThemes.theme: Perseverance and the hope of Christ’s kingdom
keyThemes.explanation: They are to make their calling and election sure, for so an entrance shall be ministered unto them abundantly into the everlasting kingdom (1:10-11).

keyThemes.theme: The reliability of the apostolic testimony
keyThemes.explanation: The apostles were eyewitnesses of his majesty and heard the voice from the excellent glory in the holy mount (1:16-18).
The word of prophecy is more sure, and no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation, for holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost (1:19-21).

2 Peter 2.summary: There were false prophets among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and many shall follow their pernicious ways, and through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you (2 Peter 2:1–3). God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell and delivered them into chains of darkness to be reserved unto judgment, and spared not the old world but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, and turned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly (2 Peter 2:4–6). He delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked, for the Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished (2 Peter 2:7–9). Chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness and despise government are presumptuous and selfwilled and are not afraid to speak evil of dignities, whereas angels bring not railing accusation against them before the Lord (2 Peter 2:10–11). These are as natural brute beasts, spots and blemishes, having eyes full of adultery, beguiling unstable souls, with an heart exercised with covetous practices, which have forsaken the right way, following the way of Balaam of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness but was rebuked by the dumb ass speaking with man's voice (2 Peter 2:12–16). They are wells without water and clouds carried with a tempest, who speak great swelling words of vanity and allure through the lusts of the flesh, promising liberty while they themselves are the servants of corruption, for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage (2 Peter 2:17–19). If after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ they are again entangled therein and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning, as in the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again, and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire (2 Peter 2:20–22).
2 Peter 2.whereWeAre: Chapter 1 ended with holy men of God who spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost (1:21). Chapter 2 warns that false teachers shall bring in damnable heresies, gives the judgments on the angels, the old world, and Sodom, and the rescue of Noah and Lot, and describes the way of Balaam (2:1-22). Chapter 3 answers the scoffers.

keyFigures.name: The false teachers
keyFigures.role: Privily bring in damnable heresies, deny the Lord that bought them, and through covetousness make merchandise of believers (2:1-3,10-19).

keyFigures.name: God and the Lord
keyFigures.role: Spared not the angels that sinned or the old world, and knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations (2:4-9).

keyFigures.name: Noah
keyFigures.role: Saved the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness (2:5).

keyFigures.name: Lot
keyFigures.role: Just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked, was delivered (2:7-8).

keyFigures.name: Balaam of Bosor
keyFigures.role: Loved the wages of unrighteousness and was rebuked by the dumb ass speaking with man's voice (2:15-16).

keyThemes.explanation: False teachers privily bring in damnable heresies, and through covetousness make merchandise of believers (2:1-3).
God spared not the angels that sinned, the old world, or Sodom and Gomorrha, so the judgment of the ungodly is sure (2:4-6,9).
The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, as he delivered Noah and just Lot (2:5,7-9).
The false teachers follow the way of Balaam, loving the wages of unrighteousness, walking after the flesh, and despising government (2:10-16).
They promise liberty while being the servants of corruption, for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage (2:17-22).

explainedReferences.explanation: Peter quotes the proverb about a dog returning to its vomit.

2 Peter 3.summary: Peter writes this second epistle to stir up their pure minds by way of remembrance, that they may be mindful of the words spoken before by the holy prophets and of the commandment of the apostles of the Lord and Saviour (2 Peter 3:1–2). There shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, saying Where is the promise of his coming, for all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation (2 Peter 3:3–4). They willingly are ignorant that by the word of God the heavens were of old, and the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished, but the heavens and the earth which are now are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men (2 Peter 3:5–7). One day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and the Lord is not slack concerning his promise, but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance (2 Peter 3:8–9). The day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, so what manner of persons ought they to be in all holy conversation and godliness, looking for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness (2 Peter 3:10–13). They are to be diligent that they may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless, and to account the longsuffering of the Lord salvation, as their beloved brother Paul hath written, in whose epistles are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction (2 Peter 3:14–16). They are to beware lest they be led away with the error of the wicked and fall from their own stedfastness, but grow in grace and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, to whom be glory both now and for ever (2 Peter 3:17–18).
2 Peter 3.whereWeAre: Chapter 2 ended with the proverb of the dog and the sow (2:22). Chapter 3 answers scoffers who ask Where is the promise of his coming, tells of the longsuffering of the Lord and the day of the Lord, and closes with a call to grow in grace and knowledge (3:1-18). 1 John follows.

keyFigures.name: Peter
keyFigures.role: Writes this second epistle to stir up their pure minds by way of remembrance (3:1).

keyFigures.name: The beloved
keyFigures.role: Told to be mindful of the words of the prophets and apostles and to grow in grace (3:1-2,17-18).

keyFigures.name: The scoffers
keyFigures.role: Walk after their own lusts and say Where is the promise of his coming (3:3-4).

keyFigures.name: The Lord
keyFigures.role: Not slack concerning his promise, but longsuffering, and his day will come as a thief in the night (3:8-10).

keyFigures.name: Paul
keyFigures.role: Our beloved brother, who hath written things hard to be understood (3:15-16).

keyFigures.name: The unlearned and unstable
keyFigures.role: Wrest the scriptures unto their own destruction (3:16).

keyThemes.theme: The reliability of God's word and promise
keyThemes.explanation: The word of God by which the heavens were of old and by which the world that then was perished is the same by which the present heavens and earth are reserved unto fire (3:1-7).

keyThemes.theme: Divine patience and the call to repentance
keyThemes.explanation: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, but is longsuffering, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance (3:8-9).

keyThemes.theme: The certainty of judgment and the coming day of the Lord
keyThemes.explanation: The day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, and the heavens shall pass away with a great noise (3:7,10).

keyThemes.theme: Holy living and hope in the new creation
keyThemes.explanation: Looking for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness, believers are to be in all holy conversation and godliness and found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless (3:11-14).

keyThemes.theme: Stability, sound understanding of Scripture, and growth in grace
keyThemes.explanation: They are to beware lest they be led away with the error of the wicked, and grow in grace and the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ (3:15-18).
